title: When Thinking Impairs Sleep: Trait, Daytime and Nighttime Repetitive Thinking in Insomnia
author: Lancee J, Eisma MC, van Zanten KB, Topper M
notes: PubMed abstract independently checked. Two studies: 139 and 64 participants. Only nighttime sleep-related worry was consistently associated with sleep impairment. Abstract-level verification; not a full-text appraisal.

title: Bedtime repetitive negative thinking moderates the relationship between psychological stress and insomnia
author: Benham G
organization: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
notes: Wiley journal abstract independently checked. 507 undergraduate participants. Stress and insomnia relationship was moderated by bedtime repetitive negative thinking, with different patterns in insomnia and non-insomnia subgroups. Observational; not causal. Abstract-level verification.

title: Cognitive factors and processes in models of insomnia: A systematic review
author: Tang NKY, Saconi B, Jansson-Frojmark M, Ong JC, Carney CE
organization: University of Warwick and collaborating institutions
notes: PubMed and open-access PMC record checked. 12 articles were included in synthesis; review identified 9 distinct insomnia models and 20 cognitive factors (39 including sub-factors). Abstract/full bibliographic record checked.

title: Sleep loss and emotion: A systematic review and meta-analysis of over 50 years of experimental research
author: Palmer CA, Bower JL, Cho KW, Clementi MA, Lau S, Oosterhoff B, Alfano CA
organization: Montana State University and collaborating institutions
notes: PubMed abstract independently checked. Meta-analysis: 154 studies, 1,338 effect sizes, N=5,717. Sleep loss reduced positive affect and increased anxiety symptoms; negative-affect findings were mixed. Abstract-level verification.

title: Does cognitive behaviour therapy for insomnia reduce repetitive negative thinking and sleep-related worry beliefs? A systematic review and meta-analysis
author: Ballesio A, Bacaro V, Vacca M, Chirico A, Lucidi F, Riemann D, Baglioni C, Lombardo C
organization: Collaborating sleep and psychology research institutions
notes: PubMed abstract independently checked. 15 randomized controlled trials. CBT-I effects on worry Hedges g approximately -0.41 to -0.71; rumination effect g=-0.13 and not reliable. Abstract-level verification.

title: Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: An American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline
author: Edinger JD et al.
notes: American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline checked. Strong recommendation for multicomponent CBT-I for chronic insomnia in adults; conditional recommendation against sleep hygiene as standalone treatment. Guideline-level verification.
